# F001 — A byte-for-byte reproduction check that includes an environment descriptor is host-bound, not evidence-bound
phase: evidence binding (this repository predates the port-* phases; nearest: port-audit)   step: n/a   date: 2026-09-02T10:20Z
what happened: `internal/portplan.VerifyOracleReproduction` regenerates the semantic-id oracle report with the pinned javac 17.0.19 and requires `bytes.Equal` with `evidence/intake/semantic-id-oracle.json`. The committed report embeds `"jdk_vendor": "Homebrew"`. On Linux with the pinned Temurin 17.0.19 the regeneration differed in that one line only, reading `"Eclipse Adoptium"`; all 969 declarations, totals and javac options were identical.
what it cost: `internal/portplan` reads red on every non-Homebrew host for a reason unrelated to the declarations the check protects; about forty minutes to isolate after two other environment gaps in the same package were closed.
where the deciding moment was: when the report's identity fields were chosen. An environment descriptor was placed inside the bytes a reproduction check compares. REFERENCE section 4 names "existence standing in for identity — a digest of the wrong thing"; this is the neighbouring form, a digest over the right thing plus an environment field.
evidence: `internal/portplan/reproduce.go` (`VerifyOracleReproduction`); `diff evidence/intake/semantic-id-oracle.json <linux regeneration>` = one hunk, `jdk_vendor`; recorded in `.claude/CLOUD-ENVIRONMENT.md` "Known environment failures" and as an owner decision in `.claude/GOAL-LOOP.md` P0.
bin: NEW RULE candidate — a reproduction check compares only what the pinned toolchain determines; environment descriptors are recorded beside the compared bytes, never inside them. Not yet filed against the family (this session cannot push to mike-skills).
